title: Model availability forecasting workbench & prospect prioritizer
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Goal: Build a lightweight forecasting workbench that aggregates model availability signals (provider uptime, variant deprecation notices, pricing changes, quantization readiness) and produces a prioritized list of procurement prospects for Dedicated/Private capacity. Deliverables: 1) ETL for daily model-supply signals, 2) time-series forecast models (short horizon 7/30 days + risk indicator), 3) priority scoring UI in the Console with drilldowns, 4) integration with procurement runbook to trigger reserved-capacity experiments. Success metrics: precision@10 for 'at-risk' models >= 0.75 over 30 days; lead time improvement for procurement decisions >= 14 days; decreased emergency fallback incidents by 20% in pilot orgs.
acceptance_criteria: - Daily ingestion pipeline running with >= 95% success rate to internal data lake (S3). - Forecasting model produces confidence intervals and risk label for each model variant. - Console view displays top 25 prospects with source attribution and SLA delta. - Team runbook mapping prospect -> procurement action defined and validated with Solutions team. - Pilot completed with 2 enterprise accounts and success metrics tracked in dashboard.
comments: 2026-02-19: Kickoff w/ Eng (Priya Kapoor) + DS (Miguel Santos). Agreed to source signals from provider status pages, public pricing APIs, telemetry (token volume spikes), and GitHub releases. Action: Eng to prototype scrapers (ENG-5012).

2026-02-25: Early architecture review. Decision: use incremental daily snapshot (not streaming) to keep compute costs low; keep schema extensible for new signals (e.g., geo-region outages). Tradeoff: small lag vs cost. Priya flagged potential rate-limits on provider APIs — added backoff logic.

2026-03-02: DS prototype results: naive ARIMA baseline shows signal for sudden availability drops but underestimates recovery windows. Miguel proposes ensemble with changepoint detector. Added estimate for DS work (5 points).

2026-03-05: Design review with Leah Morgan. Console mockups: compact scoreboard + timeline heatmap + 'why this prospect' explanation panels. Leah requested inline links to contract terms and regional latency impact. Mockups uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Model+Availability+Workbench

2026-03-10: Integration plan: procurement automation will create a procurement task in Hub for prospects with risk>=0.8. Solutions engineering to validate runbook. Draft runbook: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1Pbq-example-runbook
